understanding: This is a reflection+design task, NOT implementation. I must audit each of the 16 weaknesses (plus the contracts principle) from tmp/memory-weakness-analysis.md against the REAL memory code (verified directly: lib/memory.ps1, lib/project-context.ps1, lib/codemem.ps1, librarian.ps1, tools/memory-tail.ps1, driver/20-context.ps1, driver/84-loop-reply-markers.ps1, config.json), classify each as (a) already closed / (b) partial / (c) really hurts, then pick exactly 2-3 high-leverage improvements that REUSE existing mechanisms (typed memory, trust/status, freshness, librarian, evidence-fields) without adding new layers/validators. The deliverable is a durable PLAN file in decisions/ with a 16-row table + atoms; the operator checks integrity, 'no new mechanism', and atom smallness. Code-verified reality: typed memory + trust/status + a typed/mixed project-context pack ALREADY exist; the freshness subsystem ALSO exists but is INERT because (1) records almost never carry evidence.sha1 (ConvertFrom-ProjectMemoryMarker stores sha1 only if the agent typed it; no auto-compute) and (2) restaleOnSha1Mismatch/verifyOnRecall are absent from config.json so Test-MemoryHitFreshness returns true early. Retention is uniform (no kind/source rules; dedup/prune protect only pinned). No memory heartbeat, no recall-replay, no global context budget.
summary:
The analysis's main thesis is correct and the code confirms it: the leverage is NOT new checks but activating and structuring mechanisms that already exist. The single highest-leverage move is auto evidence-enrichment, because it switches ON an entire dormant subsystem (lazy freshness on recall) that is already coded but currently a no-op. I choose 3 atoms, each a small modification to an EXISTING function (no new file/layer/validator), collectively reusing all five named mechanisms: (1) auto evidence/sha1 enrichment at marker write [reuses evidence-fields + freshness]; (2) trust/authority labeling in the semantic recall render + 'code is source of truth' framing [reuses typed memory + trust/status]; (3) kind/source-aware retention inside the librarian helpers [reuses librarian + typed memory], which closes W3 and W12 together. The 16-row audit table to embed in the plan file:

| # | weakness | status | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | mixes trust levels; needs authority hierarchy | b | Typed kind/trust/status fields + project pack already render by kind-section; BUT generic Get-MemoryRecall is a flat '%-only' list and trust is never shown to the agent. Gap = labeling in the semantic block -> ATOM 2. |
| 2 | auto-memory saves conclusions, not deltas | b/c | Get-MemoryDistilled stores a free-text 'fact' with no evidence anchor; Update-ProjectMemoryAfterTask keeps commit in meta only. Partly mitigated by ATOM 1 (enrichment) + ATOM 2 (worklog!=truth label); deeper redesign deferred. |
| 3 | task-memory clutters recall; retention by source | c | Invoke-MemoryAgePrune is UNIFORM (age+importance+unused); Search-Memory filters only by tag/status. No source TTL -> ATOM 3. |
| 4 | freshness depends on agent-typed sha1 | c | CONFIRMED keystone: ConvertFrom-ProjectMemoryMarker stores sha1 only if typed; no auto-compute; restale/verify flags absent in config.json so Test-MemoryHitFreshness no-ops -> ATOM 1. |
| 5 | detached memory-tail dies silently | c | memory-tail.ps1 writes nothing on start/finish/error; no status.json. Cheapest NEW item; recommended fast-follow (advanced_version), not in core 3. |
| 6 | semantic recall fetches similar-not-needed; mixed recall | a | Already closed: Get-ProjectContextPack does rule-based typed recall (facts/risks/invariants/tests/decisions) + semantic + code + decisions + skill/anti-skill. Priority 5 essentially done. |
| 7 | memory self-conflict; supersede model | c | Set-MemoryStatus has active/stale/rejected/archived only; no superseded_by/subject/predicate. Real but needs NEW fields+logic = new mechanism -> deliberately deferred. |
| 8 | code memory stale separately | b | Index-CodeBase already does manifest-sha1 incremental reindex; BUT Get-CodeRecall shows no index-freshness/timestamp warning in prompt. Partial; minor. |
| 9 | decisions read directly, not all vectorized (OneDrive) | b | librarian ingests decisions/*.md idempotently but SKIPS reparse-point files (the exact OneDrive case); no normalized cache. Niche; deferred. |
| 10 | fast-lane too blind | b/c | No dedicated minimal safety pack found. Orthogonal to memory-mechanism reuse; deferred. |
| 11 | agent markers irregular; mandatory candidates block | b | Markers parsed (84-loop-reply-markers -> Add-ProjectMemoryFromMarker); auto-gate Add-TaskMemory is the safety net so memory isn't marker-only. No end-of-task candidate block; medium leverage; deferred. |
| 12 | librarian deletes rare-but-important; protected classes | c | Invoke-MemoryDedup/AgePrune protect ONLY pinned; project_decision/invariant/test unprotected -> folded into ATOM 3. |
| 13 | no recall-quality eval / replay tests | c | None found. Real but test-infra, lower per-line leverage; deferred. |
| 14 | memory discourages reading live code; confidence format | b/c | Get-MemoryRecall has no per-entry confidence/'code is truth' framing -> folded into ATOM 2. |
| 15 | too many sources duplicate; context budget manager | b/c | Format-Transcript concatenates ~11 sources each with its OWN char cap, but NO global budget/eviction. Real but bigger refactor; deferred. |
| 16 | principle: contracts not checks (Foundation #2) | a | Already the design philosophy; all 3 chosen atoms strengthen existing contracts (evidence-backed authority, retention-by-kind) rather than adding checks. |

7-priorities evaluation (asked explicitly): P1 authority-levels = PARTIAL (typed sections exist in project pack; missing in semantic recall + trust unshown) -> ATOM 2, cheap. P2 auto-evidence-enrichment = MISSING, CHEAPEST high-leverage because building blocks (Get-ProjectFileSha1/Resolve-ProjectEvidencePath/Get-FileSha1) exist and it ACTIVATES the dormant freshness path -> ATOM 1. P3 lazy-freshness-only-recalled = ALREADY HAVE (Set-MemoryHitsLastRecalled + Format-ProjectMemoryHits -RequireFresh), just inert -> fed by ATOM 1, zero new code. P4 retention-by-kind/source = MISSING (uniform prune) -> ATOM 3. P5 mixed-recall = ALREADY HAVE (project pack). P6 one memory_status heartbeat = MISSING, cheapest purely-NEW (one file in memory-tail) -> advanced_version fast-follow. P7 replay-tests = MISSING, deferred. Cheapest overall among the four asked: lazy-freshness is free (already built); among the genuinely-missing, auto-evidence-enrichment is the cheapest AND highest-leverage keystone.

decision_atoms.statement: ATOM 1 (keystone): auto evidence/sha1 enrichment at marker write. file=lib/project-context.ps1 (ConvertFrom-ProjectMemoryMarker / Add-ProjectMemoryFromMarker). change: when evidence has 'file' but no 'sha1', resolve the path via existing Resolve-ProjectEvidencePath, compute sha1 via existing Get-ProjectFileSha1/Get-FileSha1, and backfill sha1+commit+line_text into the evidence object before Add-ProjectMemory. acceptance: a [[PROJECT_FACT: ... | file=lib/memory.ps1 | line=1043]] written WITHOUT sha1 lands with evidence.sha1 populated; after that file changes, the recalled entry is flagged stale by the EXISTING Test-MemoryHitFreshness. reused-instead-of-new: evidence-fields + the already-built freshness subsystem (Test-ProjectMemoryFreshness, Format-ProjectMemoryHits -RequireFresh, lazy-on-recall) — no new validator. risk: low (best-effort, wrapped try/catch; no-file markers behave exactly as today).
decision_atoms.reason: Verified that the freshness machinery is fully coded but a no-op because records lack sha1 and config flags are off. One small wiring change at the single write-site activates the whole dormant path — maximum leverage per line, and it is exactly the analysis's P2 with the cheapest cost.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Adds a file read + git lookup at write time (post-task, detached path — not on the hot loop), and only enriches marker-written project memory, not the LLM auto-gate output (acceptable: markers carry file refs, the gate does not).

decision_atoms.statement: ATOM 2: trust/authority labeling in the semantic recall render. file=lib/memory.ps1 (Get-MemoryRecall; mirror in Get-AntiSkillRecall framing). change: prefix each rendered hit with its existing kind/trust (via the already-present Get-MemoryKind/Get-MemoryTrust) e.g. '[worklog/observed]' vs '[fact/verified]', and add ONE header line 'подсказка, не истина; код — источник правды; worklog/hypothesis проверять по файлам'. acceptance: the semantic recall block visibly separates verified/evidence-backed entries from worklog/low-trust ones, and renders the disclaimer; project pack sections unchanged. reused-instead-of-new: typed memory + trust/status fields already stored on every record — pure render change, no schema/layer. risk: low (formatting only; falls back to current output if fields absent).
decision_atoms.reason: Directly answers the analysis's #1 thesis and P1 (memory passing off worklog/hypothesis as fact) at the cheapest possible layer — the prompt render — reusing fields the records already carry. Also closes W14 (overconfidence) with the same change.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Slightly longer recall block (a few chars/entry + one header line); does not give a full 4-section AUTHORITATIVE/EPISODIC/HYPOTHESIS/SKILL split (the project pack already provides the typed structure, so a second split would duplicate, not add).

decision_atoms.statement: ATOM 3: kind/source-aware retention inside the existing librarian helpers. file=lib/memory.ps1 (Invoke-MemoryAgePrune + Invoke-MemoryDedup). change: treat a small protected set (project_decision, project_invariant, project_test) like pinned for SILENT deletion — never drop them via age-prune or semantic-dedup (status transitions still allowed); and let task:* / memory_note kinds prune more aggressively (shorter effective TTL). No new function; same call-sites in librarian.ps1. acceptance: a low-importance project_invariant survives age-prune and survives a near-duplicate dedup against a worklog; a stale task:normal note older than its TTL is pruned. reused-instead-of-new: librarian (Invoke-MemoryAgePrune/Invoke-MemoryDedup already wired) + typed memory kinds — strengthens the existing prune, adds no new pass. risk: medium (touches deletion logic) — mitigated because the change only makes deletion MORE conservative for authoritative kinds, reducing data-loss risk, the inverse of adding risk.
decision_atoms.reason: Closes W3 and W12 in one atom by reusing the librarian. Code confirms dedup/prune protect only 'pinned', so a rare project_invariant can be silently deleted today — exactly the analysis's protected-class concern.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Adds a kind check inside two loops; if importance defaults shift later, the protected-kind list must stay in sync (kept tiny and explicit to bound this).

decision_atoms.statement: Explicitly DEFER (this pass) the heavier items to honor 'no new mechanisms / small atoms': supersede subject/predicate (W7 — needs new fields+conflict logic), recall-replay harness (W13 — new test infra), global context-budget manager (W15 — cross-source refactor), code-index freshness banner (W8), decisions normalized cache (W9), fast-lane safety pack (W10), end-of-task candidate block (W11). Record them in the plan as a 'next-pass / fast-follow' list, with the single memory_status.json heartbeat (W5/P6) named as the cheapest fast-follow.
decision_atoms.reason: The operator specifically reviews for atom smallness and non-proliferation; bundling these would violate both. Naming them keeps the audit honest (every weakness has a verdict) without committing to new layers now.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Leaves W7/W13/W15 open for now; accepted because each would introduce a new mechanism or a large refactor, against the task's core constraint.

decision_atoms.statement: Deliverable shape: write ONE durable plan file under decisions/ (e.g. decisions/<dec-id>/memory_weakness_audit_plan.md) containing the 16-row table above + the three atoms each with fields {файл, изменение, acceptance, что переиспользуешь вместо нового, risk} + the 7-priorities evaluation + an explicit 'no new layers/validators introduced' statement. Do NOT modify any memory code in this task.
decision_atoms.reason: Matches output_format and the success tests exactly (16-row table, 2-3 atoms with the five atomic fields, priorities evaluation, code-verification evidence, no implementation).
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Plan-only means the leverage is unrealized until a follow-up implementation task; acceptable and required by the contract (task_type=architecture, 'НЕ реализуй').

assumptions: The 'memory code' referenced by the contract maps to the files I verified: lib/memory.ps1, lib/project-context.ps1, lib/codemem.ps1, librarian.ps1, tools/memory-tail.ps1, driver/20-context.ps1, driver/84-loop-reply-markers.ps1, config.json — and code, not the analysis, is ground truth.
The 16 rows correspond to the analysis's numbered items 1-16, where #16 (the contracts principle) is rendered as a principle row rather than a discrete defect — yielding the required 16-row table.

'7 priorities' = the seven improvements listed in the analysis's final formula (section 19); the four to evaluate (authority-levels, auto-evidence-enrichment, lazy-freshness-recalled-only, one heartbeat) are a subset.
restaleOnSha1Mismatch and verifyOnRecall are intentionally absent (off-by-default) in config.json today; enabling them is part of activating freshness but is a config flip, not a new mechanism.
Enriching at the marker write-site is sufficient for leverage because file-anchored evidence comes from markers, not from the LLM auto-gate (which distills prose).

risks.risk: Auto-enrichment computes sha1 against the wrong path/repo (project channel vs bridge root) and writes misleading evidence, or slows the post-task write.
risks.mitigation: Reuse the existing Resolve-ProjectEvidencePath (already channel/scope-aware) and Get-ProjectFileSha1; best-effort try/catch that leaves evidence untouched on failure; runs only on the detached memory-tail path, off the hot loop.

risks.risk: Retention change (ATOM 3) over-protects and lets authoritative-kind noise accumulate, or a kind typo silently disables protection.
risks.mitigation: Protected set is a tiny explicit allow-list (3 kinds); protection blocks only SILENT deletion, status (stale/superseded) transitions remain; pair with the existing dedup so true duplicates still collapse by importance among non-protected records.

risks.risk: Operator judges the set as still doing 'too much' or an atom as not truly small.
risks.mitigation: minimal_version ships only ATOM 1+2 (both single-function render/wiring changes reusing freshness+trust); ATOM 3 and the heartbeat are explicitly optional/advanced. Every atom names the existing function it edits and the mechanism it reuses.

risks.risk: Activating freshness surfaces many 'stale' flags at once (because nothing was enriched before), startling the agent/operator.
risks.mitigation: Enrichment is forward-only (new writes); old records stay no-sha1 -> treated as 'hint, verify', unchanged behavior; staleness only appears once a freshly-enriched file actually changes.

minimal_version: ATOM 1 (auto evidence/sha1 enrichment in ConvertFrom-ProjectMemoryMarker/Add-ProjectMemoryFromMarker) + ATOM 2 (trust/authority labeling + 'code is source of truth' line in Get-MemoryRecall). Two small changes to existing functions, reusing evidence-fields, the dormant freshness subsystem, and typed-memory trust/status. Together they make recalled facts evidence-backed and visibly ranked by trust — the two highest-leverage, lowest-risk lines in the analysis — with zero new files/layers/validators. Delivered as a plan-only decisions/ file (no code changes in this task).
advanced_version: minimal_version + ATOM 3 (kind/source-aware retention in Invoke-MemoryAgePrune/Invoke-MemoryDedup, protecting decision/invariant/test from silent delete, aggressive TTL for task:*; reuses librarian) + fast-follow: a single memory_status.json heartbeat written by tools/memory-tail.ps1 on start/finish/error (cheapest purely-new item, reuses the existing detached writer + Write-AtomicFile) surfaced in /memory. Plus a documented 'next-pass' backlog for the deferred heavier items (supersede subject/predicate W7, recall-replay harness W13, global context-budget manager W15, code-index freshness banner W8) — each flagged because it would add a new mechanism/refactor and therefore is intentionally out of this pass.
